You are helping with a retrospective analysis of a code review session. Your job is pure extraction and reporting — read specific files and report back structured facts. Do not judge quality yourself; that happens after you report back.

## Context

A Claude Code session (transcript file below) ran the `zimmerMANNReview` skill against PR #74 on the `zimmermann-pwa` repo (a Salesforce PWA Kit storefront project). This is Marcel's own PR (SFCC-91, PDP colour swatches), being reviewed by a separate, independent session as an arms-length audit. The session dispatched three agents: `zm-tester` ("Audit PR #74 code quality angles"), `zm-orchestrator` ("Scope verdict for PR #74 vs SFCC-91"), and `zm-scorer` ("Verify PR #74 audit findings" — this is zm-scorer running in "findings mode," verifying claims as CONFIRMED/PLAUSIBLE/UNSUPPORTED, not scoring the PR itself).

## Files to read

Main session transcript (large, 3.8MB — do NOT read the whole thing in one pass; use targeted reads/greps first to find the relevant sections, then read specific line ranges):
`/Users/marcel.a.n.navarro/.claude/projects/-Users-marcel-a-n-navarro-Dev-zimmermann-pwa/e25d570c-0d1b-42fa-8f1e-f67f905a3c08.jsonl`

Three subagent transcripts (also potentially large):
`/Users/marcel.a.n.navarro/.claude/projects/-Users-marcel-a-n-navarro-Dev-zimmermann-pwa/e25d570c-0d1b-42fa-8f1e-f67f905a3c08/subagents/agent-ad6dfa97b3cde0845.jsonl`
`/Users/marcel.a.n.navarro/.claude/projects/-Users-marcel-a-n-navarro-Dev-zimmermann-pwa/e25d570c-0d1b-42fa-8f1e-f67f905a3c08/subagents/agent-a46f072baeab4f22d.jsonl`
`/Users/marcel.a.n.navarro/.claude/projects/-Users-marcel-a-n-navarro-Dev-zimmermann-pwa/e25d570c-0d1b-42fa-8f1e-f67f905a3c08/subagents/agent-afeb8ec169daf0059.jsonl`

The three `.meta.json` files next to the subagent transcripts tell you which agentType/description belongs to which file (already known: one is zm-scorer, one is zm-tester, one is zm-orchestrator — check the `.meta.json` files to map which jsonl is which if needed).

Each `.jsonl` line is a JSON object representing one turn/event. Look for `type: "assistant"` entries with `message.content` containing text (the actual reasoning/output) and `type: "tool_result"` entries for tool outputs. The final substantive report from each subagent is usually near the end of its file.

## What to extract and report back

**1. What each of the 3 agents found** — the actual findings, with their CONFIRMED/PLAUSIBLE/UNSUPPORTED or verdict labels where given. For zm-scorer specifically, report which findings it verified vs rejected/downgraded.

**2. What the parent session (main transcript) did with those findings** — did it present them to Marcel? What was the final verdict (approve, request changes, etc.)? Was anything drafted as a comment? Was anything actually posted to GitHub, or did it stay as internal analysis? Quote the final summary/conclusion the session reached, if one exists.

**3. Ground truth gates** — did the session run `tsc`/`test`/`lint`/`audit:tokens` at both head and base commits with real numbers, or did it skip/assume this? Quote the actual commands and numbers if found.

**4. Did the 3 agents converge or diverge?** Did zm-tester and zm-orchestrator find overlapping issues independently, or did their findings not overlap at all (which could mean either good coverage-splitting or a real gap between them)?

**5. Compare against known CodeRabbit findings on PR #74** (already known context, don't re-derive): CodeRabbit found on PR #74's Round 1: (a) a Storybook CI failure in the `WithoutLink` story's play function calling `getByRole('radio')` after a role was stripped, (b) a squad-ownership mismatch in `.claude/registry/pages.md` (later declined as invalid, since that file is auto-generated), (c) `handlePrevPage`/`handleNextPage` using an unclamped `pageStart` in a functional updater, (d) `isFocusable` being false for all rendered swatches when paginated away from the selected item (a WCAG 2.1.1 issue), (e) a magic string `'color'` needing a named constant. All five were already fixed in commit `54e924f` before this other session's review presumably ran (check the session's timestamps/commit references to confirm whether it reviewed the code before or after that fix commit landed). Did this session's own review (via its 3 agents) independently find any of these same 5 things on its own? Did it find anything CodeRabbit missed? Did it miss anything CodeRabbit caught (check if it reviewed a version of the code where the CodeRabbit fixes were already applied, in which case those wouldn't be there to find, which is fine — only flag as a real miss if the code state it reviewed still had the bug and its review didn't catch it)?

**6. Tone/register of any drafted comments.** If any PR comment text was drafted (even if not posted), quote it and note whether it reads naturally or has any issues (sycophancy, jargon, references to other PRs/builds that shouldn't be there, anything a fair reviewer might object to).

**7. Any moments where Marcel corrected, pushed back on, or overturned something the session/agents concluded.** Quote the exchange if found.

**8. Any moments where the session found something notably good or noteworthy that should be recorded as a positive pattern** (e.g., agents independently converging on the same real finding via different methods, a claim being properly downgraded from CONFIRMED to PLAUSIBLE with correct reasoning, etc).

Report back concisely but completely — this is going to be read by a retrospective analysis, so precision and direct quotes with context matter more than brevity, but don't paste entire raw file contents, summarize and quote only the load-bearing parts.

Base directory for this skill: /Users/marcel.a.n.navarro/.claude/skills/zimmerMANNReview

Review of a colleague's work. Same architecture as the build chain — ground truth, a gated audit,
then present and stop — tailored to a PR you did not write.

**Intended model: Sonnet 5 at maximum effort.**

**The thing that makes it work:** you hold the ground truth and the adjudication, and delegate only
the reading. Reviewers are cheap and fallible; measurements are expensive and authoritative. Keep
those on opposite sides of the line.

**Input:** `PR #74` — a PR number.

**Scale to the work.** A two-file PR does not get four reviewers. Nothing too crazy, no
overthinking.

---

## Phase 1 — ground truth. Yours, not an agent's.

### Frame the PR

Base SHA, head SHA, files changed, ±lines. **Use the live head** — a stale ref has already caused a
whole round of re-verification here.

### Requirements — Jira, Confluence, Figma

Build the same requirements picture a PreBuild would build, then judge the PR against it. Every
scope argument, every "this is missing", every "this wasn't asked for" gets decided against these
words — not the PR description's paraphrase of them.

**Jira.** Pull the full ticket: description, ACs, linked work items, and — critically — the full
comment thread. Decisions made in comments routinely contradict the description and never make it
back into the ACs. Flag: untestable ACs · requirements that contradict each other or the comments
· a linked blocker still open · a decision in comments that the implementation may not have seen.

**Confluence.** If the ticket links a PRD, TSD, or integration doc, read it. The Jira ACs are
often a summary; the full requirements live in Confluence. Flag: a Confluence requirement not
reflected in the ACs · a doc that contradicts the ticket · a doc that describes an approach the
PR does not follow.

**Figma.** Read the design systematically — not just the node cited in the PR description.

{
  "title": "Fix generateRegistry.mjs producing wrong descriptions",
  "tldr": "The registry generator script writes factually wrong descriptions for at least two entries (ShopperAgent, useMiaw) and churns unrelated consumer counts on every run — found while reviewing PR #74, but it's a pre-existing bug in the generator itself, unrelated to that PR's changes.",
  "prompt": "scripts/generateRegistry.mjs (which writes .claude/registry/components.md and .claude/registry/hooks.md, run via `npm run generate:registry` on postinstall) has at least two confirmed-wrong outputs as of the current develop tip:

- In .claude/registry/components.md, the `ShopperAgent` entry's description reads "Validates that a URL is from a trusted Salesforce domain" — that is not what ShopperAgent does (it initializes/manages the embedded messaging service). The description appears to have been swapped with some other utility's description.
- In .claude/registry/hooks.md, the `useMiaw` entry's description reads "Maps BCP-47 locales to Salesforce language codes" — also not what useMiaw does (it initializes embedded messaging when the script loads). Same apparent swap pattern.

Additionally, the generator produces unrelated churn on every run — e.g. a PR touching only PDP colour-swatch components caused ~33 lines of components.md and ~14 lines of hooks.md to change for entirely unrelated components/hooks (App, Field, Link, Register, Search, useCurrentBasket, useMultiSite, etc.), with consumer counts shifting by anywhere from ±1 to ±11 with no plausible causal link. This makes every future PR's registry diff noisy and makes real changes hard to spot in review.

Investigate scripts/generateRegistry.mjs to find why descriptions are getting mismatched to the wrong symbol (likely an indexing/ordering bug when walking the AST or matching JSDoc comments to declarations) and why consumer counts are non-deterministic between runs (possibly a caching, ordering, or glob-matching issue). Fix the generator, then regenerate both files and confirm the diff against current develop only reflects genuinely-changed entries."
}

# Retrospective Extraction: zimmerMANNReview session on PR #74 (SFCC-91 PDP colour swatches)

**Session:** `e25d570c-0d1b-42fa-8f1e-f67f905a3c08` (named "zimmermann-pwa-83"), 2026-08-31 17:39–20:37. PR #74, branch `feature/SFCC-91_pdp-colour-swatches`, base `269d5d4` → head `54e924f`, +1518/-126 across 17 files. GitHub itself reported `mergeStateStatus: BLOCKED` at fetch time. Author is `marcelannavarro` — the session flagged immediately at the start that this is Marcel's own PR, not a colleague's, and continued because "the PR itself notes a non-author human review is still required for the Tier 2 file."

---

## 1. What each of the 3 agents found

**zm-orchestrator ("Scope verdict for PR #74 vs SFCC-91") — Verdict: BLOCKED**
- Tier 1 files touched: `overrides/app/theme/foundation/colour.ts:93` (`disabled: grey[200]` added to `icon` alias) and `zimmTokens.ts:84` (`--zimm-color-icon-disabled`). Independently re-ran `gh api user --jq .login` → `marcelannavarro`, confirmed membership in `tier-1-approvers` and repo `admin` — so "legitimately pre-authorized, not a self-declared bypass," but still surfaced as a hard-stop per its own scope-guard rules since the change traces to a different Figma node than the ticket's own annotation, not to any real AC.
- All 5 real Jira ACs + the pagination annotation verified with file:line evidence (AC1 `index.tsx:223` `populated.length > 1` gate; AC2 image sourcing at `product-detail/index.tsx:923`; AC3 `aria-checked`/border via `zimmColourSwatch.css.ts:36-42`; AC4 `chakra(RouteLink)` traced to `use-variation-attributes.js:151-161`; AC5 `Boolean(value.imageUrl)` filter).
- Over-delivery finding: the `href`-absent "quick-view-modal" branch in `ZimmColourSwatch` has no live caller anywhere in this PR (traced end-to-end — no override of `product-view-modal`/`bonus-product-view-modal` exists, and base versions never call `renderVariationAttribute`).
- 3 "known gaps" (set/bundle products keep base swatch UI, no Playwright for AC4, pre-existing i18n gap) — all judged legitimate deferrals, not corner-cuts.
- Registry churn (`.claude/registry/*.md`) judged pure auto-regeneration, not flagged. Squad-ownership conflict (CODEOWNERS vs. `squadA.md`) judged pre-existing, already resolved via CodeRabbit thread, not a fresh blocker.

**zm-tester ("Audit PR #74 code quality angles")** — 8 angles + correctness/conventions/test-coverage/security sweeps, plus two throwaway falsification test probes written and executed against the real component (then deleted, working tree confirmed clean):
- 🔴 **Must-fix:** Neither new interactive recipe (`zimmColourSwatch.css.ts`, `zimmColourSwatchGroup.css.ts`) defines `_hover`, while `zimmNavItem`, `zimmTextInput`, `zimmButton`, and even base SFCC's own `swatch-group.js` all do.
- 🟡 Should-fix: stale/self-contradictory comment (`zimmColourSwatchGroup.css.ts:159-168` says "only cursor... not a design token" but the block sets a real `color` token too); missing test file for `product-view/index.tsx` despite new branching logic; silent loss of `orderable`/out-of-stock visual treatment (dropped end-to-end, no forwarding, type has no field); pagination test suite never asserts `tabindex`/`aria-checked` after an actual click; registry generator (`generateRegistry.mjs`) produces genuinely wrong descriptions for `ShopperAgent` and `useMiaw`, unrelated to this PR.
- 🔵 Notes: `href?: string` should be `string | null` (hook returns `null`, not `undefined`); single-frame stale-pagination-flash on cross-product nav flagged as PLAUSIBLE only (reasoned, not reproduced — explicitly could not force a jsdom repro).
- Independently verified via **execution, not just reading the diff**: both CodeRabbit-flagged Round-1 blockers (WCAG tab-stop, dead first pagination click) hold under real probes.
- Explicitly could not check Figma itself (no MCP tool in its toolset that session) — flagged this gap rather than guessing.

**zm-scorer ("Verify PR #74 audit findings" — findings-verification mode, not scoring)** — verified 9 findings (F1–F9) drawn from zm-tester's report:
- **CONFIRMED:** F1 (lint: reran `npm run lint` on HEAD itself, got the exact `✖ 22 problems (6 errors, 16 warnings)` and both prettier errors at the cited lines), F2 (stale comment), F3 (unused href branch — traced independently), F4 (missing `_hover`, checked all 3 sibling files), F5 (missing test file, checked both HEAD and base via `git ls-tree`), F7 (href/`null` type gap).
- **F6 downgraded CONFIRMED → PLAUSIBLE**, with explicit reasoning: the behavioural claim (orderable silently dropped) is fully reproduced, but the original claim that there's "no comment anywhere acknowledging this narrowing" overstated the record — `zimmColourSwatchGroup/index.tsx:47-49,78-80` do explicitly name the stock/orderability concept in comments justifying the *filter* decision, just not the specific disabled-affordance consequence.
- **F8 CONFIRMED**, checked the whole shipped suite (test file + Storybook `play`), not just the cited lines.
- **F9 kept as PLAUSIBLE**, matching the original's own stated confidence — deliberately did not attempt a jsdom repro (would be a false-negative given RTL's synchronous effect flushing), assessed only whether the code-structure reasoning holds up (it does).

---

## 2. What the parent session did with the findings

The parent (main) session did substantial ground-truth work **itself** before/alongside dispatching agents: pulled PR metadata, CodeRabbit's raw comment thread via `gh api`, the full Jira ticket + comment history, ran gates on both SHAs via a git worktree, independently ran the `gh api user`/`tier-1-approvers` check itself (before the orchestrator re-ran the same check independently later), did a live Figma comparison, and did a real Storybook keyboard-navigation pass (verified computed styles via JS: selected border `rgb(25,25,25)`, disabled chevron `rgb(209,209,209)`).

When zm-tester flagged the missing `_hover` state as a must-fix, the parent **did not just accept the framing** — it queried the Figma MCP tools itself (`get_metadata` on nodes `40000307-13823` and `40003328-115591`) and confirmed no hover variant exists in the design ("only Unselected/Selected/Focus × Large/Small"), downgrading the finding from a possible design-fidelity miss to "a codebase-convention question."

Adjudication was run through an explicit `AskUserQuestion` with 4 questions (pagination test gap, missing hover, stock-state signal, unused href branch) rather than free text. Marcel's answers directly shaped the final decision (see §7).

**Final state:** A full comment batch (1 general + 5 inline) was drafted and presented to Marcel with "Want me to post this batch, or adjust anything first?" **Nothing was posted.** No `gh pr comment`, `gh pr review`, or any write/POST call appears anywhere in the main transcript or any of the 3 subagent transcripts — confirmed by exhaustive grep. The session's last two exchanges were Marcel asking "what's our status then?" (answered: "Pending: just your go on posting the comment batch to PR #74 — nothing has been posted yet") and "what's the session id for this session?" — the session ends there, still awaiting go-ahead. This is correct per AGENTS.md Hard Rule #15 (never post without explicit request in the current prompt) and the skill's own design ("comments post only on his go").

No formal GitHub review state (APPROVE / REQUEST_CHANGES) was ever drafted or discussed — only a comment batch. The registry-generator bug was correctly spun off as a **separate** task (via `spawn_task`, title "Fix generateRegistry.mjs producing wrong descriptions") rather than folded into the PR #74 comment thread, since it's a pre-existing defect unrelated to this PR's own changes.

---

## 3. Ground-truth gates — real numbers, not assumed

Run via Bash directly by the parent session, HEAD in the working tree, BASE in an isolated `git worktree add --detach` (so as not to disturb Marcel's tree):

| Gate | Command | Base (`269d5d4`) | Head (`54e924f`) |
|---|---|---|---|
| TypeScript | `npx tsc --noEmit` | 0 errors | 0 errors |
| Token audit | `node scripts/auditTokenUsage.mjs` | 4 unacknowledged violations (52 files scanned) | same 4, unchanged (57 files scanned) |
| Lint | `npm run lint` | `✖ 20 problems (4 errors, 16 warnings)` | `✖ 22 problems (6 errors, 16 warnings)` |
| Vitest | `npm run test` | `Test Files 26 passed (26)` / `Tests 408 passed (408)` | `Test Files 28 passed (28)` / `Tests 433 passed (433)` |

The +2 lint errors were pinned to exact new lines (`zimmColourSwatch/index.tsx:86:17`, `zimmColourSwatch/index.test.tsx:119:30`, both `prettier/prettier`) and independently re-confirmed by zm-scorer re-running `npm run lint` on HEAD alone and getting the identical `6 errors / 16 warnings`. The 4 pre-existing token-audit violations were confirmed to be in unrelated files (`header/index.tsx`, `header.ts`, `navConstants.ts`) — correctly attributed as inherited debt, not something this PR introduced. CI's own rollup showing Playwright/BrowserStack as SKIPPED was checked and correctly attributed to AC4 having no `.feature` file yet (disclosed, gherkin-first-workflow-consistent), not a hidden red flag.

---

## 4. Convergence vs. divergence between the 3 agents

**Genuine independent convergence** (same conclusion reached via different angles, not because they were told to check the same thing):
